## Body

PASS-WITH-NOTES -- performance, round 1
PR #300; head 4ef227f6ae704ca5f3923cd2d6d00fcdc8423fa5; base 305b60ab7b81fc183402e9a485d3c0e97549f63f.

No blocking cost regression found. The changed sites retain their counters, remove two external reads, and add no periodic work. This is a cost verdict, not a substitute for the separately requested correctness/security verdicts.

Changed-site budget

| Site | Before -> after | Trigger and scaling |
| --- | --- | --- |
| omp.models | One bare-name launch -> one resolved-path launch when OMP resolves successfully | Per model inventory invocation, including observed-label resolution, not only the public catalog operation. No periodic/seat-wide fan-out. The existing 10 ms try_wait loop is unchanged: at most about 100 in-process checks/s for the existing 5 s timeout, no launches per check. |
| lsof.identity-peer-pid | One bare-name launch -> one /usr/sbin/lsof launch on macOS; cached PATH resolution elsewhere | Per host-identity ancestry check. No timer or healthy-seat polling. The launched lsof still scans socket ownership; it was not eliminated. |
| ps.identity-caller-ancestry | One whole-machine ps -> zero launches | At most 64 in-process parent-reader calls per check, constant-bounded independent of total fleet size. |
| ps.tmux-harness-process-tree | Up to two ps launches -> one /bin/ps snapshot, followed by one in-process selected-start read | Per invocation. The retained whole-machine snapshot and parsing still scale with host process count; launch count does not scale with subtree size. All production call sites pass local_start. |
| ps.registration-native-process | Unchanged: at most one single-PID argv launch per host-named ancestor per registration | Per qualifying registration on macOS, with registration-local caching and HOST_NAMES gating; Linux reads procfs. Existing holder-current refusals pay zero. Not a new poll or per-seat-per-tick launch. |
| CLI statusline_owns | Zero -> zero | Only extracts the identical observed_start(...).local closure into local_start. No launch or cadence change. |

Sources: crates/harnesses/src/models.rs:317-351,443-453; crates/daemon/src/http/identity.rs:676-738; crates/harnesses/src/proc.rs:259-280,397-416; crates/tmux/src/lib.rs:1655-1672; crates/daemon/src/registration.rs:2475-2565; crates/cli/src/main.rs:2688-2692.

Notes on the claims

1. The sensor is sound for the contiguous literal spelling it checks, not a semantic proof of every program launched through helpers/macros. The nine-crate source scan saw 197 production files, six /bin/ps literal controls, and no rejected bare literals. The real six-test spawn_sites suite passes, including count coverage, retired operations and registration gating. The new predicate catches Command::new("omp") and qualified Command::new("lsof"), but not Command::new(NAME), Command::new(concat!(...)), a literal on a separate line, or a macro forwarding $program. Existing production_lines exclusions also remain. This is a disclosed tripwire limit, not a new uncounted changed launch or a reason to require an AST framework. Sources: crates/testkit/tests/spawn_sites.rs:17-55,246-290,297-304,470-480.

2. The PR table's request triggers are narrower than the call graph. The pane walk also serves adoption (http/identity.rs:829), process-backed controls (http/mod.rs:2916), conditional recipient checks (http/governance.rs:2008-2010), and Codex caller checks until a thread is recorded (http/codex_caller.rs:48-60 -> codex_bind.rs:67-88). The latter is not the event-gated CodexBinder itself. Likewise, omp.models also serves resolve_omp_model (models.rs:443-453), not just catalog display. None introduces a new cadence here, and all pane-walk users benefit from the removed recheck launch. State rates per invocation/request rather than assuming these operations occur only at registration.

3. "Resolved once" means a successful cached hit, with the existing resolver's recovery semantics. A missing executable is not cached and returns the bare name; a vanished hit is resolved again and ENOENT can retry once. Relative PATH entries also retain their path spelling. The PR reuses this established behavior rather than adding a permanent absolute-path guarantee for every OMP failure case. The macOS identity lsof constant is unconditionally absolute. Sources: crates/core/src/program.rs:97-117,134-162; http/identity.rs:735-738.

Registration F-item decision

No new F-item justified by these readings. The retained C27 exception is still correctly host-gated and unchanged by #300. At the baseline, 235 ps launches belonged to 124 registration attempts: heartbeat.pane.unchanged 73/187 (2.562 ps each), receive.pane.unchanged 12/28, explicit.pane.* 7/16, two retired pane attempts 2/4, lease-retry.pane.holder-current 24/0, unspecified.pane.retired 6/0. Across the 94 attempts that paid argv cost this is 2.50 ps/attempt, not a universal 2.6 constant. Both registrations and ps were flat during the measured minute. The nonzero daemon CPU while registration launches were zero cannot be assigned to argv reads. Do not introduce a PID/start-only argv cache: exec can change argv without changing those keys. Reopen C27 only with measured registration latency/CPU harm, as its ruling requires.
